metaTitle: TimeHabit — Plan your day, protect your focus
metaDescription: A planner, focus timer, and screen time manager for iPhone and iPad, with a little help from Huahua the panda.
heroBody: Plan your tasks, schedule and habits. Focus on one thing at a time, and set limits for the apps that pull you away. Huahua the panda is here for all of it.
preview: 6.0 preview · iPhone & iPad, iOS/iPadOS 17 or later. The App Store currently offers 5.1.4.
heroAlt: TimeHabit 6.0 Today screen with sample tasks, progress and a Focus shortcut.
guideTitle: A little help through your day
guideBody: Four ways to get started in TimeHabit 6.0.
todayDesc: See tasks, scheduled events and habits together. Give each one just enough structure to get started.
today2: Choose a task, event or habit. Add a due date, time or goal as needed.
today3: Check off a task or log a habit right from Today.
todayAlt: Today screen with a list of sample tasks and habit cards.
focusTitle: Give one thing your full attention
focusDesc: Start a free focus session or track the time you spend on a specific task.
focus1: Tap Focus in Today, or tap the clock next to a task.
focus3: Start focusing. You can pause when you need to and review the time logged afterward.
focusAlt: Focus setup with a 25-minute countdown and a hand-drawn bamboo grove.
limitsDesc: Block selected apps during a particular time, set a usage limit or schedule a break. The usage report helps you see where your screen time goes.
limits1: Open Limits and connect Apple Screen Time.
limits2: Tap + and choose a rule, such as Scheduled limits.
limits3: Pick the apps and time window, then save your rule.
limitsAlt: Limits screen with the Screen Time connection, add button and tools.
reviewTitle: See how your time adds up
reviewDesc: Look back on your day, see how you spent your time by tag, or keep a short journal entry.
review1: Open Review and select a date in the calendar.
review3: Open the ··· menu for tag analysis, Inbox or Journal.
reviewAlt: Review screen with a monthly calendar and a daily timeline.
privacyIntro: This policy describes TimeHabit 6.0 and this product page.
localBody: TimeHabit works without a Linutech account. Your plans, habits, journal entries, selected images, focus records and app-limit settings are stored on your device. TimeHabit does not upload them to Linutech servers or use them for advertising or tracking.
screenBody: With your permission, TimeHabit uses Apple Screen Time to apply app rules and show usage reports. The usage reports are processed by an on-device Apple Screen Time extension. You can choose whether to allow notifications, Face ID for app access, or Apple Health access to read step counts and save focus sessions as mindful minutes. You can manage permissions in system settings.
externalBody: When you request a link preview, your device contacts the website. If your version offers calendar subscriptions and you enable one, your device contacts the calendar source you chose. Those services handle the requests under their own policies. Apple processes purchases and restores; TimeHabit uses Apple’s transaction information to determine your access.
backupBody: TimeHabit 6.0 does not automatically sync your records through iCloud. You choose where exported files and backups are saved. You can delete records in the app and remove its local data by deleting it. Exported files and copies held by your storage provider are managed separately.
webBody: This page does not use advertising trackers, analytics or cookies. GitHub Pages hosts it and logs visitor IP addresses for security. Links to Apple and other sites are covered by their respective privacy policies.
contactBody: If you email Linutech, we receive your address, message and any attachments you send so we can respond. You can use the same address for privacy questions and requests concerning information you sent us.
sceneHint: Pick a sticker to flip through Huahua’s day
todayDetail1Body: Tap the tiny panda beside Today. The overview stays pinned while you scroll through the day’s tasks, events and habits. Tap the panda again to collapse it.
todayDetail2Title: Swipe right to edit or delete
todayDetail2Body: Swipe a task card to the right to reveal the pencil and trash buttons. Swipe left or tap outside to close the actions. Deleting a recurring task may offer a choice between this occurrence and the series.
todayDetail3Title: Check off a task or a step
todayDetail3Body: When the swipe actions are closed, tap the task card or its circle to complete it. Tap a completed task to reopen it. Expand a task’s checklist to mark individual steps.
todayDetail4Title: Move an overdue task to today
todayDetail4Body: Under previously unfinished tasks, tap Do Today on the task you want to move. It changes the plan date and leaves the task open.
todayDetail5Title: Record a habit and adjust the details
todayDetail5Body: Tap a habit’s record control in Today. Check in for a simple habit or enter your progress for a quantity goal. Open the habit record to edit the amount or add a note.
todayDetail6Title: Keep a task as a reusable template
todayDetail6Body: In the task editor, open the ··· menu and choose Save as template. To reuse it, choose Create from template in the editor, check the draft and save the new task.
focusDetail1Body: Tap the clock on its card to record focus time against that task. If that task already has an active session, the same clock takes you back to it.
focusDetail2Title: Adjust the timer before you start
focusDetail2Body: Choose stopwatch to count up, countdown to work for a set duration, or Pomodoro to alternate work and breaks. In the setup, tap the duration or Pomodoro settings to change them.
focusDetail3Title: Set up sound and app protection
focusDetail3Body: Open the focus settings before you start. Choose a sound and, if you want screen time protection, choose which apps to block or allow. Protection for this session starts with the timer.
focusDetail4Title: Hide the timer while it runs
focusDetail4Body: Tap the top-left close or collapse control to leave the focus screen. The timer keeps running. Tap Focus in Today again to return to it.
focusDetail5Title: Pause, end, or finish the task
focusDetail5Body: Use Pause to take a break and Resume when you are ready. End closes the current session. In task focus, Complete Task is the separate action for marking the task done.
focusDetail6Body: Open Review → ··· → Analysis → Focus. Choose a day, week, month or year to see sessions and time totals in that period.
limitsDetail1Body: Choose apps to restrict and a lock duration when you want to start a period of uninterrupted work immediately.
limitsDetail2Body: Pick days and time windows for recurring boundaries, such as weekday bedtime. You can add more than one time window to a schedule.
limitsDetail3Body: Give the selected apps a shared time allowance. TimeHabit applies the restriction when the allowance is used up.
limitsDetail4Body: Set how many temporary openings the rule will approve and how long each opening lasts. Use the rule’s temporary-use action to request an opening.
limitsDetail5Body: Choose an action to complete first, such as a task, a habit or a focus session. Set which apps the rule will open and for how long.
limitsDetail6Body: Choose how long you can use the selected apps in one round and how long they should stay locked while you take a break.
limitsDetail7Title: Find temporary use inside the rule
limitsDetail7Body: Tap a rule card to open its details. If that rule allows it, choose Request temporary access. From the same page, you can tap End access now to finish early.
limitsDetail8Body: Open a rule to see its selected apps, settings and current status. Use the edit control to adjust it. If it asks you to reconnect or reselect apps, follow the prompt on that rule.
limitsDetail9Body: In Limits, find Tools → Usage time to see app activity. Open Review → Analysis → Focus for the time you logged in focus sessions.
reviewDetail1Title: Switch between a day and a month
reviewDetail1Body: Use Day or Month at the top of Review. Choose a date to see that day’s timeline, or use the arrows beside the date to move through the current view.
reviewDetail2Body: Tap ··· → Analysis. Switch among day, week, month and year. Tap the displayed period to jump to a specific date or range. Use the Focus tab for focus totals.
reviewDetail3Title: Write a journal entry with a panda stamp
reviewDetail3Body: Tap ··· → Journal. Select a day and tap the notebook icon. Pick a stamp, write your entry, and save it. In the editor you can add a mood, tags, images or links.
reviewDetail4Title: Write a quick note or find an older entry
reviewDetail4Body: In Journal, tap the pencil to write a brief note. Swipe the paper styles at the bottom to choose one. Tap the magnifying glass to search your saved journal entries.
reviewDetail5Title: Capture an idea and turn it into a plan
reviewDetail5Body: Tap ··· → Inbox and save an idea or link. Open the item’s menu and choose Convert to turn it into a task or event when you know what to do with it.
reviewDetail6Title: Go back to a record from the journal
reviewDetail6Body: Tap an event record or habit note shown in the journal’s daily notes to open that source record. Use the date in Journal to jump to another day.
